newsitem.title: USA: US stocks to open higher, lifted by book-to-bill.
newsitem.headline: US stocks to open higher, lifted by book-to-bill.

text.p: Wall Street stocks should open higher on Tuesday, lifted by several factors, including strength in technology stocks after an industry gauge of semiconductor demand came in strong.

The Dow industrials should also benefit from a report that Westinghouse Electric will announce a spin-off of its industrial operations. Short-covering and Friday's expiration of options could also add to the opening, analysts said.
Standard & Poor's December futures rose 1.25 to 735.35. The long bond was up 6/32 to yield 6.49 percent.
"It looks like we're going to have another higher opening. It's almost hard to believe after the past week," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The Dow Industrials surged 36 to about 6256 on Monday, its fourth consecutive record closing high, which came on the heels of last week, the second biggest weekly point gain ever.
"The Westinghouse news is very positive for the Dow. (Westinghouse) could rise a few points," he said. Westinghouse is one of the components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
The Nasdaq also looked poised to start the day strong after setting a new all-time record of 1263 last night.
"The book-to-bill was very strong. That's really going to help chips stocks and technology stocks in general," he said.

The Semiconductor Industry Associations's closely watched book-to-bill report came in at 1.10, beating bullish expectations of 1.0. Overnight, shares of technology companies traded in Japan, South Korea, the Netherlands and London all rose after the index's strong results.

"We also have options expiration and with the strong gains of the past two days, we're also seeing a lot of short-covering. But I think somewhere along the line today, we're going to be hit by some profit-taking," Cardillo said.

At 1000 EST/1500 GMT, the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, one of the 12 Fed banks, is due to report its indices which monitor manufacturing and service-sector activity. But analysts are much more concerned about the upcoming release of two key inflation indicators.
The U.S. Producer Price Index is due to be released tomorrow, with the Consumer Price Index following on Thursday.
Tokyo stocks moved higher, boosted by the strong finish in U.S. equities and the semiconductor data. The Nikkei 225 rose 141 to 21,206.
The FTSE 100 rose in London, up 15.4 to 3929.8.

The dollar was mixed in Asian trading, firmer against the yen but steady against the German mark. It rose in later European trading to about 1.50 marks after comments by an official from Germany's central bank.
Corporate boards should seat no more than six and should hire more outside directors, a commission will report today, according to the New York Times MarketPlace column.
United Auto Group's vice chairman Marshall Cogan must steer the company's stock price back uphill, the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street reports.
